reasoning: A hybrid strategy combines autonomous reasoning to quickly identify plausible shared features based on domain knowledge and structural patterns, while using external XAI tools to quantitatively validate feature importance and detect spurious correlations. This ensures both interpretability and robustness in identifying features that are statistically salient but semantically irrelevant to the target label. The combination leverages human-in-the-loop reasoning with data-driven attribution to uncover spurious signals.

autonomous_tasks.query: Identify which features are common across all misclassified instances (13590 and 21096) and assess whether any features are present in all instances despite being semantically unrelated to income prediction.
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: List of shared features across instances, with notes on their semantic relevance to the target class (income)

autonomous_tasks.query: Why might 'workclass=Local-gov' or 'marital-status=Married-civ-spouse' be misleading or spurious in this context, even if frequently appearing in misclassified cases?
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A reasoned hypothesis about why these features may act as spurious signals due to underlying data biases or correlations with other variables

tool_selection.reasoning: SHAP provides global feature importance with interpretability, helping identify which features have high influence across the misclassified set. Integrated Gradients offer gradient-based attribution that captures the model’s internal decision paths, revealing whether high importance stems from meaningful signals or spurious correlations. Sensitivity Analysis directly tests whether turning off a feature changes prediction outcomes, thereby confirming its spurious nature. Together, these tools validate and quantify shared spurious features beyond mere presence.
